title: Love Fragments
program_note:
Love Fragments, written for and commissioned by Grace Cloutier, sets fragments of poems by William Shakespeare, Robert Desnos, and Alexander Pushkin to music.  Each poem presents a different reaction to the disappointments of love.  Shakespeare shows us the despair of a one-sided love in which the protagonist has given all there is to give.  Desnos unfolds a series of reactions to an unresponsive lover:  obsession, anger, leading to a murderous rage but eclipsed at the end by abject devotion.  Lastly Pushkin pushes abject devotion one step further, to the point where the protagonist would be content with a feigned or pretended love.  Through it all, we get a view of love that is broken—fragmented—beyond repair.

After a short tear-filled introduction, the Shakespeare setting begins in an almost-Elizabethan style, direct and mournful.  The Desnos setting, with its seething passion, is far more turbulent and energetic.  As that almost-frantic energy expends itself, we turn to the Pushkin setting.  While the vocal line is filled with minor-mode melodic motifs, it is set against an accompaniment that echoes the despair of the Shakespeare setting and the tears of the opening in a way that underscores the permanent fracture and sense of loss created in the protagonist’s heart.

The duration is approximately 12 minutes.

David S. Lefkowitz

19 April, 2014

Los Angeles, CA
